33.43091,-96.33861: Trenton. The earliest Anglo settlers in this area, drawn to the fertile farmlands, probably came to the locality known as Wildcat Thicket in the mid-1800s. 33.43259,-96.33899: First National Bank of Trenton. Founded in 1901 by John Donaghey, J. B. Robinson, and Y. B. Reed -- major officers for 33 years. Descendants still operate institution. 33.43271,-96.33807: First Methodist Church of Trenton. In 1887 members gathered at the Union Church in Trenton to organize the Methodist Episcopal Church, South. The first pastor was the Rev. W. J. 33.43403,-96.22131: Grove Hill. The earliest settler in this area was George w. Smith, a native of Georgia, who moved here in 1844. 33.43603,-96.47582: James P. Dumas. (1820-1875) Born in South Carolina. In 1841 married May Thompson and moved to the Republic of Texas. 33.43605,-96.32034: Burns Cemetery. Land for this cemetery was donated in 1876 by Tennessee native William Boyd Burns (1821-1907), whose log cabin home was located adjacent to the site. 33.43678,-96.1675: Ashley Lodge No. 681, A. F. & A. M.. Chartered on December 12, 1889, this was the seventh Masonic lodge organized in Fannin County. 33.43986,-96.4837: Old Town of Cannon. Founded 1852 by Elijah Cannon, who came from South Carolina with his children and slaves, to develop 700 acres of land. 33.44004,-96.42488: Pilot Grove. Founded in early 1850s. On Bonham-McKinney Stage Line. Called Lick Skillet; renamed, 1858, for J. P. Dumas' Ranch. 33.44139,-96.42453: Pilot Grove Baptist Church. This congregation traces its history to the establishment of the United Baptist Church here in 1848 on 3.5 acres of land donated by Hezakiah Warden. 33.44887,-96.14938: Portland. The earliest known settler in the Portland community was Jesse Green London (1843-1875). 33.45653,-96.16892: First Baptist Church of Bailey. On May 23, 1888, a small group of neighbors met together at the home of Mr. and Mrs. Baywood Atkins to discuss forming a Baptist church. 33.46191,-96.40153: Bethel Baptist Church. This congregation grew from an early prayer group, established in the Bethel community in 1875. 33.47104,-96.0903: Gober Public Schools. The town known as Gober was settled in the 1840s, and was first called Grittersville. 33.47167,-96.08964: Gober Baptist Church. This congregation was organized on August 4, 1889 by the Rev. S. P. Clement and twelve charter members. 33.47266,-96.19342: James Fowler Biggers. (January 21, 1829 - October 26, 1914) A native of South Carolina, James Fowler Biggers grew up in Mississippi. 33.48438,-96.26645: Buchanan Cemetery. Alexander Buchanan (1796-1846), his wife Delilah (1806-1870), and their eleven children moved to the Republic of texas from Illinois in 1844. 33.49048,-96.02962: Site of Bartley-Woods School. Several rural schools existed in Fannin County in the 1890s, including Bartley School and Woods School. 33.49306,-96.25102: Lindsey-Randolph Cemetery. Tennessee native Thomas Lindsey (b. 1794) brought his family to this part of Fannin County in 1837.
